correctness.rationale: For the regular dodecagon, coordinate sign/interchange symmetries imply the published symmetric-Minkowski-plane classification of all unit isosceles partners, y=±Rx. The sign choice gives the same quotient, while dihedral symmetry and reflection reduce all unit pairs to one half-edge 0≤a≤1/2. An independently implemented symbolic check verified that each of the six absolute facet expressions is bounded by the stated candidate on EVERY relevant affine interval: the unit-edge expression; A=||x+2Rx||; C=||x+Rx||=||x−Rx||; B0=||2x+Rx|| for 0≤a≤q; B1 for q≤a≤1/2. Each inequality follows exactly from its endpoint values, and an active signed facet identically equals each candidate. q=(5−2√3)/13 is in (0,1/2) and the two B branches agree there. Exact differentiation independently verified the submitted derivative identities; the first is strictly positive except at a=0 and the second strictly positive throughout, so the maximum is the midpoint a=1/2. Direct substitution yields A=B=√3+1/2, C=(1+√3)/2 and Ω=14/5−√3. All 12 vertex quarter turns were checked symbolically. Unlike finite grids, affine dominance and derivative proofs cover every real parameter in the interval.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021–2022 Ω source was materially read at the definition, examples and complete symmetric-Minkowski reduction; it establishes the reduction but does not evaluate the regular dodecagon. The 2019 primary regular-4n-gon paper was inspected at its unit-isosceles rotation theorem and regular-polygon constants, which use different functionals and predate this Ω. The candidate record itself appeared as a Resultary search self-match, which is excluded from priority evidence. No independent exact dodecagonal Ω table or logically dominating theorem was found. The unique active switch, monotonic reduced profile, exact value and equality orbit are thus original to best documented knowledge, not the general structural reduction. value.rationale: The regular dodecagon is a canonical non-Hilbert symmetric Banach plane and Ω is a previously defined geometric invariant, so the object and question have independent motivation. The exact value is not a mere relabeling of a known table: an exhaustive 12-facet comparison produces a genuine active-facet switch at q=(5−2√3)/13, the complete two-branch reduced profile, a strict monotonicity theorem and a unique maximizing symmetry orbit at edge midpoints. The contrast with the octagonal Ω vertex maximizers shows a geometrically meaningful difference, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The precise fact is an independently useful calibration of normed-plane orthogonality geometry and its polyhedral facet dependence, though it neither solves all regular polygons nor supplies a large downstream theorem.
